intended_object: The domain of the infinitesimal (Stone) generator of a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group U(t) on a complex Hilbert space: D(A) = {ψ ∈ H : lim_{t→0} (U(t)ψ − ψ)/(it) exists}, as a ℂ-subspace. The docstring, the module documentation and its use as the domain of the `LinearPMap` `generator` all say this.
explanation:
The carrier is the set of ψ for which there is an η with `genDiffQuot U ψ t = (I*t)⁻¹ • (U t ψ − ψ)` tending to η as t → 0, t ≠ 0. That is the punctured neighbourhood `𝓝[≠] 0`, which is the right filter for a difference quotient. This is exactly the standard domain of the Stone generator. The factor 1/i does not change which vectors belong: the limit of (U(t)ψ−ψ)/(it) exists exactly when the limit of (U(t)ψ−ψ)/t exists. The submodule closure proofs (sum, scalar multiple, zero) are routine and correct.

The definition is not too narrow. The ambient structure, a strongly continuous unitary group on a complex Hilbert space, is the standard setting of Stone's theorem, and the i-normalisation, chosen so that the generator is self-adjoint, belongs to that setting. One could define generators of C₀-groups on any Banach space, but Mathlib has no such notion (a search for semigroup or unitary-group generators found nothing). This object is the specific Stone-generator domain the library needs.
